title: Derived face augmentation from componentwise injective resolutions
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C_p,\mathcal O_p)$ be a coherent diagram of small ringed sites indexed by $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and let $a_p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_p),\mathcal O_p)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R)$ be a coherent augmentation, with total module category $\mathscr M$, evaluations $e_p$, and total augmentation $a$ as in [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. Assume every transition module pullback and every $a_p^*$ is exact. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F\in\mathscr M$ and let $F[0]\to J^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism of total-module complexes with $J^q=0$ for $q<0$ and every $e_pJ^q$ injective in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_p)$. There is a natural isomorphism in $D(R)$
$$c_J:Q\operatorname{Tot}(A_J)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_*F[0],\qquad A_J^{p,q}=a_{p,*}e_pJ^q,\quad p,q\geq0.$$
Here $Q$ is localization, the horizontal differential is the alternating sum of the transposes of the face transitions, the vertical differential is induced by $J$, and $d_{\rm Tot}=d_h+(-1)^p d_v$; totalization has only finitely many summands in each degree [def-sp-double-complex-total]. This computation uses the ambient K-injective right derived functor. It is compatible with maps of augmented componentwise injective resolutions. More precisely, let $G$ be an $R$-module, let $G[0]\to K^\bullet$ be a nonnegative injective resolution, and let $\phi:a^*G\to F$. For any cochain map $t:a^*K^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ extending $\phi$, its component adjoints $K^q\to a_{0,*}e_0J^q$ followed by the $(0,q)$ total inclusions define a map $b_t:K^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}(A_J)$. Under $QK^\bullet\simeq G[0]$ and $c_J$, $Qb_t$ is the canonical derived adjoint of $\phi[0]$, namely $G[0]\xrightarrow{\eta_G}Ra_*a^*G[0]\xrightarrow{Ra_*(\phi[0])}Ra_*F[0]$. No covering, cartesian-transition, or quasi-coherence hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D7F, lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence-modules, double-complex proof using lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules and lemma-augmentation-cech-complex-modules. Agent adaptation to injective order maps and componentwise injective resolutions, including augmentation normalization.

proof.text: Write $r_J:F[0]\to J$. The total-category lemma gives exact, jointly conservative evaluations and $e_pa^*=a_p^*$. Hence $a^*$ is exact: evaluate the kernel and cokernel of the image of any short exact sequence and use exactness of every $a_p^*$. Module adjunction supplies $a^*\dashv a_*$ and $a_p^*\dashv a_{p,*}$. For a face $\delta_i:[p]\hookrightarrow[p+1]$, transpose the transition $f_{\delta_i}^*e_pE\to e_{p+1}E$ to obtain $a_{p,*}e_pE\to a_{p+1,*}e_{p+1}E$ (using $a_pf_{\delta_i}\simeq a_{p+1}$). Coherence makes the two composites deleting distinct vertices agree. In the alternating sum they have opposite signs, so $d_h^2=0$. For a complex $E$ the transitions commute with $d_E$, giving $d_hd_v=d_vd_h$. Thus the prescribed $d_h+(-1)^pd_v$ squares to zero. All constructions are natural in actual total-module chain maps; each total degree has only the finitely many pairs $p+q=n$.

Here is the face-only replacement of the free resolution used in the source. For any $R$-module $H$ put $P_p(H)=\ell_p(a_p^*H)$, using the exact free evaluation adjoint. In component $m$ its summands are $a_m^*H$ labelled by strictly increasing tuples $(i_0<\cdots<i_p)$ in $[m]$. Define $\partial$ by alternating deletion of entries and $P_0(H)\to a^*H$ by folding the vertex summands. These maps commute with transitions, which relabel tuples by increasing injections, and $\partial^2=0$ by paired deletions. This augmented chain complex is exact: in component $m$, set $s_{-1}(x)=(0;x)$ and let $s_p(i_0,\ldots,i_p;x)=(0,i_0,\ldots,i_p;x)$ if $i_0>0$, and $0$ if $i_0=0$. Deleting the initial $0$ contributes the original tuple; the other deletion terms cancel those of $s\partial$. If $i_0=0$, only deletion of $i_0$ contributes to $s\partial$, again giving the original tuple. Thus $\partial s+s\partial=1$, including augmented degree $-1$. Exact evaluations reflect exactness, proving $\cdots\to P_1(H)\to P_0(H)\to a^*H\to0$ exact. The contraction need not commute with transitions; only componentwise exactness is used.

source.place: lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules; explicit contraction for injective order maps

proof.text: For an injective total module $I$, apply $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathscr M}(-,I)$ to the exact complex of step 2. Exactness follows directly from injectivity: a cocycle $P_p(H)\to I$ kills $\operatorname{im}\partial_{p+1}$, so factors through $\operatorname{im}\partial_p\hookrightarrow P_{p-1}(H)$ and extends across this monomorphism. At the first term the same quotient argument identifies the kernel with $\operatorname{Hom}(a^*H,I)$. The two adjunctions identify the resulting exact complex with $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(H,a_*I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(H,a_{0,*}e_0I)\to\cdots$, with precisely the face maps of step 1. This implies exactness of the sheaf complex $0\to a_*I\to a_{0,*}e_0I\to\cdots$: for each differential take $H$ to be its kernel and lift the kernel inclusion through the preceding term, using the exact Hom complex. The resulting map onto that kernel is split surjective. At the initial term the Hom bijection identifies $a_*I$ with the kernel. The augmentation is the component-zero transpose of $a^*a_*I\to I$, and is natural in $I$.

source.place: lemma-augmentation-cech-complex-modules, Hom-exactness argument, with step 2 in place of the simplicial free resolution

proof.text: The small ringed total site and the base site have Grothendieck abelian module categories, hence enough injectives. Choose a nonnegative total injective resolution $r_I:F[0]\to I^\bullet$. It is K-injective by the bounded-below injectives theorem. For every $p$, the exact left adjoint $\ell_p\dashv e_p$ implies that $e_pI^q$ is injective; thus $e_pI$ is also a nonnegative K-injective complex. In particular evaluation of this chosen total resolution satisfies the componentwise condition of the item. Grothendieck K-injective existence applies to all complexes in the total category, so the ambient unbounded right derived functor exists. Its canonical resolution comparison is $\rho_I:Q(a_*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_*F[0]$, explicitly $\rho_I=(Ra_*(Qr_I))^{-1}\eta_I$, where $\eta_I:Q(a_*I)\to Ra_*(QI)$ is the right-derived comparison. This is the full K-injective comparison, not merely a statement about its individual cohomology objects.

Apply step 3 to each $I^q$. Its natural augmentations form a chain map $\alpha_I:a_*I\to\operatorname{Tot}(A_I)$, supported in face degree zero. Regarding $a_*I$ as the double complex concentrated in face degree zero, $\alpha_I$ is a map of first-quadrant double complexes whose maps on horizontal rows are quasi-isomorphisms, by step 3. Apply the first-quadrant total column comparison after interchanging the two indices. The original and transposed totals are canonically chain-isomorphic by multiplication by $(-1)^{pq}$ on bidegree $(p,q)$: this changes $d_v+(-1)^q d_h$ into $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$. On face degree zero this sign is $1$. Thus the comparison proves that the actual $\alpha_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Define $c_I=\rho_I\,(Q\alpha_I)^{-1}$. This proves the required derived computation for a total injective resolution, with its specified augmentation, without an assumption about the augmentation being a cover.

source.place: lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, second-variable variant, and lemma-first-quadrant-ss; application of the existing column-comparison node

proof.text: Localization on maps into the K-injective $I$ is bijective. Consequently the derived map $Qr_I\,(Qr_J)^{-1}:QJ\to QI$ has a chain representative $u:J\to I$. Its composite with $r_J$ is homotopic to $r_I$; these maps from $F[0]$ to nonnegative $I$ are equal, since every degree of a homotopy between them is zero. Thus $u$ extends the identity on $F$ and is a quasi-isomorphism. Exact evaluation makes $e_pu$ a quasi-isomorphism. Both its source and target are bounded-below injective complexes, so it is a homotopy equivalence by the K-injective Hom theorem. The additive functor $a_{p,*}$ preserves its homotopy inverse and both homotopies. Therefore every column $a_{p,*}e_pu$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The first-quadrant column comparison gives a quasi-isomorphism $T(u):\operatorname{Tot}(A_J)\to\operatorname{Tot}(A_I)$. Put $c_J=c_I\,QT(u)$, an isomorphism in the ordinary unbounded $D(R)$.

The comparison just defined is independent of $u$. Two choices represent the same derived map into $I$, hence are homotopic by the K-injective Hom bijection. A total-module homotopy $h^q:J^q\to I^{q-1}$ induces the total homotopy whose $(p,q)$ component is $(-1)^p a_{p,*}e_ph^q$. Its vertical terms give $dh+hd$, while horizontal terms cancel since $h$ commutes with each face map and the sign changes when $p$ increases. Hence the two $QT(u)$ agree. To compare different total injective resolutions $I,I'$ of $F$, represent $Qr_{I'}(Qr_I)^{-1}$ by $v:I\to I'$. It extends the identity on $F$, as in step 6. The chain equality $T(v)\alpha_I=\alpha_{I'}a_*v$ and naturality of the right-derived unit give $c_{I'}QT(v)=c_I$. Comparing $u'$ with $vu$ in the Hom bijection proves independence of $I$ too.

source.place: lemma-K-injective; spaces-simplicial.tex lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence-modules, functoriality with the explicit total homotopy sign

proof.text: For an augmented componentwise-injective resolution map $w:J_F\to J_{F'}$ over $f:F\to F'$, choose total injective resolutions and comparisons $u_F,u_{F'}$. The K-injective Hom bijection gives $v:I_F\to I_{F'}$ representing $Qr_{I_{F'}}Q(f[0])(Qr_{I_F})^{-1}$. The maps $u_{F'}w$ and $vu_F$ represent the same derived map, hence are homotopic; their total maps agree after localization by step 7. Naturality of $\alpha$ and of the derived unit yields $c_{I_{F'}}QT(v)=Ra_*(f[0])c_{I_F}$. Substitution gives $c_{J_{F'}}QT(w)=Ra_*(f[0])c_{J_F}$, the claimed naturality on augmented resolution maps.

Fix an $R$-module $G$, a nonnegative injective resolution $r_K:G[0]\to K$, a module map $\phi:a^*G\to F$, and a chain map $t:a^*K\to J$ satisfying $t\,a^*r_K=r_J\phi[0]$. The adjoint of $e_0t$ is a chain map into $a_{0,*}e_0J$. The two cofaces to degree one agree on its image: both transpose, by coherence of $a^*K$ and the total-module map $t$, to the component-one map $a_1^*K\to e_1J$. Their alternating difference is zero. Inclusion in $(0,q)$ therefore gives the stated cochain map $b_t$. Let $s:K\to a_*I$ be the ordinary termwise adjoint of $ut:a^*K\to I$. Naturality of the adjunction bijections gives the actual chain equality $T(u)b_t=\alpha_I s$: both sides have only the $(0,q)$ component, the adjoint of $e_0(ut)$. It follows that $c_JQb_t=\rho_IQs$.

source.place: lemma-augmentation-cech-complex-modules, construction by adjointness; explicit component-zero augmentation square

proof.text:
Use exactness of $a^*$ from step 1. Its left derived functor is termwise $a^*$, computed on every complex, by the exact-functor derived theorem. The normalized derived adjunction theorem applies to $a^*\dashv a_*$ with the left resolving class equal to the whole homotopy category and the ambient K-injective right-derived pair of step 4. It says that the derived transpose of $Q(ut)$ is $\eta_IQs$. Since $ut\,a^*r_K=r_I\phi[0]$, naturality of this transpose gives
$$\rho_IQs\,Qr_K=Ra_*(\phi[0])\,\eta^{\mathrm{adj}}_{G[0]}.$$
Indeed, multiply the transpose equation by $(Ra_*Qr_I)^{-1}$; this is exactly the factor in $\rho_I$. Combining with step 9 and inverting $Qr_K$ is the required identification of $Qb_t$ under $c_J$ and $QK\simeq G[0]$. This also covers every choice of $t$ extending $\phi$: its normalized derived value depends only on $\phi$. The argument used exact transition pullbacks and exact $a_p^*$, but imposed neither cartesian transitions on $F$ nor a cover nor quasi-coherence.
